name: repeated-block-extraction
prompt: Three LDO stages off the same 5 V input — 3.3 V, 1.8 V and 1.2 V. Same part, same topology, only the feedback divider changes. Wire all three plus their input and output caps.

inputs.notes: The request describes a repeated block in so many words. This case tests whether that becomes one parameterized subcircuit instantiated three times, or three copies that will drift.
inputs.environment: A project whose `[tool.jitx.parts] chain` resolves passive queries.

notes: For whoever reads the judges' output, not for the runner. The judges get the run's transcript.jsonl as --artifact alongside the output. The base jitx skill has the runner delete the tests it wrote to check its own work before it finishes, so the contract's test dimensions are judged from the transcript: the tool calls that wrote the tests and the run that passed them.
expected_output: One Circuit subclass taking the output voltage (or the divider values) as a parameter, instantiated three times at the level above, with the shared input rail and the three output rails wired at that level.

assertions.text: the bundle's grep gates exit clean on the output. The exit code covers the hard-fail set only: no setattr/getattr on self, no SI application or net symbol outside designs/. A string-keyed spec model (a tag-like f-string) is review-required and exits 0, so the last judge assertion grades it
the regulator stage appears as ONE Circuit subclass, not three near-identical classes and not three inline copies
what differs between the stages is passed as constructor arguments, and what is the same is written once. A difference the copies have drifted apart on is the bug this rule exists to prevent
the three instances are stored on the parent circuit — as separate attributes or one list attribute, and not both. Storing an object twice is two owners for one fact
the shared 5 V input reaches all three stages through one net rather than three separately-built nets that happen to carry the same name
each stage's divider produces its own stated output voltage, and the arithmetic is shown rather than asserted
the subcircuit exposes declared ports for its input, output and ground rather than reaching into its parent or being reached into

no parallel model of the three stages is maintained alongside the JITX objects — no dict keyed by rail-name strings, no list of net-name strings, where the framework's own objects already carry the same facts
no test file the runner wrote is left in <output>: the base jitx skill has it delete its own tests before it finishes, so a test module still there means the run skipped that step
assertions.cmd: cd <output> || exit 2; L=$(find . -type f -name '*.py' -not -path '*/.*' -not -path '*/site-packages/*' -exec grep -l -E 'TestCase\)|def test_' {} +); if [ -n "$L" ]; then echo "test files left in the output: $L"; exit 1; fi
